capabilities.target: Third-party enrichment API (billed per call, shared key and quota)
Researcher sub-agent, which can itself spawn further researchers
CRM account record fields (industry, size, headquarters)

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows (internal CRM export, 40,000 rows)

instructions.note: 'Keep going until every row is complete' with no cap on retries or spawned sub-agents guarantees unbounded resource consumption for the roughly 3 percent of rows that can never return a complete result.
The only check on retry/spawn behavior is the model's own judgment of what looks 'incomplete'; no structural step count, retry count, recursion depth, or spend limit is enforced outside the model.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota (shared with sales and marketing)
Spawned researcher sub-agent(s), which can themselves spawn further researchers
Account data sent to enrichment vendor per lookup call
Nightly CRM row batch entering agent context

controls.name: Maximum retry count and sub-agent recursion depth/count limit
controls.decay_rationale: Would be enforced by the orchestrator/scheduler outside the model, so it would not weaken as model capability grows.

controls.name: Hard per-run and per-day spend/call budget cap on the enrichment API key
controls.decay_rationale: A billing/gateway-enforced cap that halts calls once exceeded does not depend on the model's behavior.

controls.name: Dedicated enrichment API key/quota, separate from the key shared with sales and marketing
controls.decay_rationale: Isolating the credential limits blast radius regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Spend/usage alert on the enrichment account before quota exhaustion
controls.decay_rationale: A monitoring threshold enforced outside the model detects runaway usage regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Dead-letter queue for rows that fail validation after N attempts, routed to human review
controls.decay_rationale: Routing persistently failing rows out of the retry/spawn loop is enforced by the pipeline, not the model.

findings.title: Unbounded retries and recursive sub-agent spawning against a shared, uncapped enrichment quota (spend-loop pattern, TC6-style) cause cross-team denial of service

forecast.watch_signal: The row source for in.crm_rows expands beyond internal CRM exports (for example, externally submitted web-form leads) or moves from a bounded nightly batch to continuous ingestion, without any step, retry, or spend limit being added first.

evidence.observation: There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents. Sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call; the API key and its monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing, whose tools stop working once the quota runs out until the next month.
Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch have malformed company names that never return a complete result, guaranteeing repeated retries and spawns every night.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

"If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account. Keep going until every row is complete." gives no stopping condition for rows that can never be completed.

recommendations.action: Enforce a maximum retry count per row and a maximum recursion depth/total count for spawned researcher sub-agents, at the orchestration layer.
Add a hard per-run and per-day spend/call budget on the enrichment API key, enforced outside the model (API gateway or billing threshold that halts further calls).
Give the enrichment agent a dedicated API key/quota separate from the key shared with sales and marketing, so a runaway loop cannot block other teams.
Add a spend/usage alert on the enrichment account that notifies a human before the shared quota is exhausted.
Route rows that fail validation after a fixed number of attempts (for example, malformed company names) to a dead-letter queue for human review instead of infinite retry or spawn.

stride_coverage.rationale: No external peer or protocol authenticates to this agent in the described design; it only invokes an internal paid API tool and spawns internal sub-agents, with no identity spoofing vector described.
The agent has no configure capability and no described mechanism for its own prompt, config, or tool definitions to be modified at runtime.
Artifacts do not describe whether individual lookup, spawn, or write actions are logged with an attributable identity or timestamp.

The only data sent externally is internal-sensitivity firmographic fields (industry, size, headquarters) sent to the enrichment vendor as the documented, intended function; no confidential or restricted data is read or transmitted.

The agent exercises only the single shared enrich_lookup credential it was provisioned with; it does not gain access to sales or marketing's own systems or credentials beyond consuming shared quota, which is captured as denial of service.
Researcher sub-agents are spawned internally by the parent agent in the same trusted runtime; no external identity claims are presented, so spoofing does not apply.
No capability allows sub-agents to modify the parent agent's configuration, prompts, or tool definitions.
Artifacts do not state whether individual sub-agent spawns or their actions are attributed to a traceable record.
Sub-agents perform the same bounded enrich_lookup research actions as the parent, handling only internal-sensitivity firmographic data with no broader disclosure vector described.
Spawned researchers inherit the same shared enrichment credential and tool scope as the parent; no mechanism is described that grants them broader privileges.
Artifacts do not describe how the enrichment API endpoint's identity (TLS, certificate pinning) is verified for cap.enrich_lookup calls.
Artifacts do not describe vendor-side logging or receipts that would let the organization attribute billed calls to specific accounts or rows.
The agent has no capability to modify the quota configuration or API key itself; it can only consume quota via calls, which is the denial_of_service concern captured in the finding.
Artifacts do not describe how the shared API key is stored or whether the agent process could expose it.
Artifacts do not describe validation applied before writing enrichment results to CRM fields, so whether low-confidence or incorrect data could be written is unclear.
CRM write only adds internal-sensitivity enrichment fields already sourced from the vendor response; it does not expose CRM data externally.
Artifacts do not describe CRM write throughput limits or whether 40,000 nightly writes could affect CRM system availability.
Artifacts do not state whether enrich_lookup responses are validated or transmitted over an authenticated, encrypted channel before being treated as trusted enrichment data.
This flow carries only internal-sensitivity firmographic fields to the enrichment vendor as the documented purpose, consistent with the agent-level information_disclosure rationale.

rating.rationale: The design has a single dominant finding: the prompt instructs the agent to retry or spawn recursive researcher sub-agents 'until every row is complete,' with no cap on steps, retries, runtime, or spend, against a per-call-billed enrichment API whose key and monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing. Because roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch can never return a complete result, this loop is guaranteed to run every night, and with no spend alert in place it can exhaust the shared quota and silently break other teams' tools (ASI08 cascading failure / denial of service). This is a missing-property finding (no retry, spawn-depth, or spend limit) rather than a malicious attack path, so per rubric 5a it is capped at 'high' rather than 'critical' even after the autonomy modifier. No declared controls exist to bring residual below that floor; all five recommended controls are recorded as missing. If the row source later expands to include externally submitted or untrusted data (data_scope_expansion) or task horizons lengthen further, the same missing limits would combine with an untrusted source into a complete lethal-spend-loop path, which is why the forecast rises to 'critical.' The single control whose absence moves the forecast most is a hard, structurally enforced spend/call cap on the enrichment API key independent of the model's own retry judgment.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; actual production behavior (true retry counts, realized monthly spend, and whether quota exhaustion has occurred) was not verified.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or billing data were provided; capability scope and credential scope (for example, for cap.crm_write) are inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on exact financial exposure is lower than confidence on the structural gap (absence of any step, retry, or spend limit), which is explicitly stated in the artifacts.
